clue.text: Red-headed half-wit upset baby with grandeur

indicators.note: upset tells us the letters of the two words that follow are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone simple-minded and ginger knocks over a baby with great pomp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' shuffles the twelve letters of BABY and GRANDEUR together; 'with' only joins the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's title character is a simple, red-haired youth caught up in the Gordon Riots.

clue.text: Pravda writer's book given to Welsh character

parts.note: Mark Renton is the narrator of Irvine Welsh's novel Trainspotting

explanation.surface: A Russian newspaper journalist's book is handed to someone from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' looks like it means from Wales, but it is the novelist Irvine Welsh. Pravda is not the newspaper but a 1985 satirical play.
explanation.definitionFit: Howard Brenton co-wrote the stage satire Pravda with David Hare.

clue.text: Lover more worked-up by submissive lover

indicators.note: worked-up means agitated, so the letters of more are stirred into a new order

parts.note: O is the submissive heroine of the erotic novel Story of O

explanation.surface: A passionate person grows more agitated beside a meek partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked-up' rearranges MORE into ROME; 'by' just places the letter beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young Montague is the archetypal ardent suitor.

clue.text: An orator messing around with escaped prisoner

indicators.note: messing around suggests the letters of an orator are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A public speaker fools about in the company of a runaway convict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaped prisoner' points to Trollope's short story Aaron Trow, not a real convict; 'with' is the usual one-letter abbreviation here.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron Trow is the convict who breaks out of jail in Trollope's short story of that name.

clue.text: Place seen on the up by Earl Buchanan's alma mater

indicators.note: in a down entry, on the up means the word for place is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lay something is to place it
E is an abbreviation for Earl in titles of peerage

explanation.surface: A location noticed rising alongside a nobleman named Buchanan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earl Buchanan' looks like one name, but the definition is Tom Buchanan of The Great Gatsby; LAY turned upwards gives YAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitzgerald tells us Tom Buchanan had been a famous football player at this New Haven university.

clue.text: People like Peter Nazareth and Angus Batty

indicators.note: batty means crazy, so the letters of and Angus go haywire

explanation.surface: Folk such as a writer named Nazareth and a man called Angus Batty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angus Batty' reads as a person's name, but 'Batty' is the anagram signal working on AND ANGUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Nazareth is a novelist and critic born in Uganda, so he is an example of its nationals.

clue.text: Tale-telling sibling lacking levity in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing says the word for lacking levity is said out loud and heard as another

parts.note: grim means stern and humourless

explanation.surface: A brother who tells stories is far too serious when listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob and Wilhelm, the German brothers, collected and published folk stories.

clue.text: Fungus, say, in toilet English guy covers up close to lavvy

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: covers up means the English guy wraps around and conceals another letter

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of lavvy is wanted

explanation.surface: A mould growing in a lavatory, which an Englishman hides near the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fungus' looks like mould, but it is Fungus the Bogeyman, the title of Raymond Briggs's picture book. Lavvy is British slang for lavatory; its last letter Y sits inside E and MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Briggs's green, smelly hero Fungus is one of a race of these goblins.

clue.text: Disintegrating house beginning to scare theatre staff

parts.note: Poe's House of Usher splits apart and sinks into the tarn at the end of his tale

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the first letter of scare

explanation.surface: A crumbling building starts to frighten the people who work at a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disintegrating' looks like an anagram signal, but the phrase points to Poe's story The Fall of the House of Usher.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the attendants who show audience members to their seats.

clue.text: Gem cut by son and a daughter of Sister Gudule

indicators.note: cut by means the gem is split open with the son placed inside

parts.note: an emerald is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A jewel being cut by a boy and a girl belonging to a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gem cut' suggests a jeweller; 'cut by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hugo's Notre-Dame de Paris the recluse Sister Gudule turns out to be the gypsy girl's mother.

clue.text: One dishonestly persuades those such as Shakespeare

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
to con someone is to swindle or trick them into something

explanation.surface: A single person tricks people into believing he is Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare is a revered cultural figure, a symbol of English literature.

clue.text: Doctor Who sounds like someone who's irritating!

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the word for an irritant is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a thorn in one's side is an annoying person

explanation.surface: Asking which Time Lord resembles an annoying person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' looks like the television series; 'Who' simply links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Thorne is the village physician who gives his name to Trollope's novel.

clue.text: A plot stopped by mother with European woodworker

indicators.note: stopped by means the mother plugs a gap in the plot

parts.note: a bed is a plot in a garden
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A conspiracy foiled by a mother and a carpenter from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' reads as a scheme, but it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's title hero is a village carpenter.

clue.text: Leaders of NFL are done in royally, scoring low points

indicators.note: leaders of takes the opening letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Football league teams are thrashed royally and score few points.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point reached, the bottom of a decline.

clue.text: "But thou, false guardian of a charge too good, / Thou, mean — of thy brother's blood!" ("Elegy to the Memory of an Unfortunate Lady", Alexander Pope)

definitions.text: "But thou, false guardian of a charge too good, / Thou, mean — of thy brother's blood!" ("Elegy to the Memory of an Unfortunate Lady", Alexander Pope)

parts.words: "But thou, false guardian of a charge too good, / Thou, mean — of thy brother's blood!" ("Elegy to the Memory of an Unfortunate Lady", Alexander Pope)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: the missing noun is the word Pope used for one who abandons his kin

explanation.walkthrough: The poem's guardian uncle forsook his niece, so the word for the gap is someone who abandons a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope's line names the uncle as one who has abandoned his own family's blood.

clue.text: Nurse having way with a politician and son impresses

parts.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse
ST is short for street, a way
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A nurse gets her own way with an MP and his son.
explanation.definitionFit: To enstamp is to stamp or imprint something, pressing a mark into it.

clue.text: "Then to the great court with its marble yard / Whose emptiness gave him —" ("Orpheus Alone", Mark Strand)

definitions.text: "Then to the great court with its marble yard / Whose emptiness gave him —" ("Orpheus Alone", Mark Strand)

parts.words: "Then to the great court with its marble yard / Whose emptiness gave him —" ("Orpheus Alone", Mark Strand)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: the missing phrase is Strand's idiom for a shiver of unease

explanation.walkthrough: The empty marble yard of the underworld unnerves Orpheus, so the gap wants an idiom for a feeling of dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Strand's empty underworld court fills Orpheus with fear and revulsion, a nervous shudder.

clue.text: Firm with debt must get a head of logistics like Talos?

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a loss is money owed or gone, a debt on the books

indicators.note: head of asks for the first letter of logistics

explanation.surface: A company in debt needs a logistics chief, says the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Talos is the setter's pseudonym, but in Greek myth Talos was a giant bronze man guarding Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical bronze guardian was huge, a giant automaton.

clue.text: Elinor's family tree displayed in democratic club

indicators.note: displayed in puts the tree inside the democratic club

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A family tree is put on show in a political club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family tree' reads as a genealogy; 'family' is part of the definition and 'tree' is ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Elinor is the elder sister in Austen's Sense and Sensibility, with that surname.

clue.text: Bessy Tulliver was one academic receiving order

indicators.note: receiving means the academic takes in the order within his letters

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
the DSO is the Distinguished Service Order

explanation.surface: A woman who was once a scholar is given a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Mill on the Floss Mrs Tulliver was born into the proud family of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bessy Tulliver's maiden name places her among Eliot's snobbish clan of sisters.

clue.text: Live catch knight brought inside for Elizabeth?

indicators.note: brought inside places the knight within the other letters

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
to net something is to catch it
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A live catch with a knight brought indoors for Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth is the heroine of Pride and Prejudice, second of the five sisters with that surname.

clue.text: Man enthralled by those like Fanny Hill in literature etc.

indicators.note: enthralled by means the man is captivated, held inside the others

parts.note: Fanny Hill is the prostitute heroine of John Cleland's novel, so one of the tarts
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man is captivated by the heroines of erotic fiction in books.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature, music, painting and drama together make up the creative disciplines.

clue.text: Creditor wound up Mangiafuoco at his workplace

indicators.note: wound up means twisted round, so the letters of creditor are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A lender is angered by a fire-eater at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Mangiafuoco (Fire-eater) is the puppet-showman in Collodi's Pinocchio, who runs his own theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangiafuoco runs and manages the puppet theatre that Pinocchio wanders into.

clue.text: Conservative Party needs leader changed? That's novel!

indicators.note: needs leader changed says the word for party swaps its opening letter for another

parts.note: a bash is a party

explanation.surface: The Tory party demands a new leader, which would be unheard of!
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'new', but the definition is J. G. Ballard's 1973 book.
explanation.definitionFit: J. G. Ballard's notorious book about car-crash fetishists has that one-word title.

clue.text: British series with Tyneside man depicting Dickens

parts.note: a row is a series of things in a line
Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: A British serial set in Newcastle portrays Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Hablot K. Browne, known as Phiz, illustrated many of Dickens's novels.

clue.text: Carnation-loving wit is uncivilised, I'm told

indicators.note: I'm told says the word for uncivilised is heard rather than read

parts.note: wild means untamed or savage

explanation.surface: A humorist fond of flowers is said to be rough-mannered.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar was the celebrated Irish humorist who wore a green carnation.

clue.text: Success was one of his stomach-turning goals

indicators.note: stomach-turning means only the middle of the word for goals is turned round

parts.note: aims are goals

explanation.surface: Victory came from a revolting goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stomach-turning' reverses only the middle pair, IM, so AIMS becomes AMIS. Success is a 1978 novel by Martin Amis.
explanation.definitionFit: Success is the novelist Martin's third book.

clue.text: Old and wicked character of Euripides?

parts.note: both wicked and mega are slang for excellent

explanation.surface: An ancient villain in a Greek tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a figure in a play, but it is a letter of Euripides's Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the last letter of the Greek alphabet in which Euripides wrote.

clue.text: Spooner said Michael and Ridgeley promoter's a cockney

indicators.note: Spooner said means the starting sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley were the pop duo Wham!
a seller promotes and pushes goods

explanation.surface: A Spoonerism about a pop duo's promoter being from London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens speaks in a famous East End London dialect.

clue.text: Pests host let off in novel by Carpentier

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or bad, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Pests are let loose by a host in a Cuban novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Alejo Carpentier's 1953 novel Los pasos perdidos is known in English by this title.
